name: Lipid Storage Disease

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient lysosomal enzyme activity specific to lipid metabolism
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with lipid storage disorders
Presence of lipid-laden macrophages or storage cells in tissue biopsy
Characteristic clinical manifestations consistent with lipid accumulation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of enzyme deficiency or pathogenic genetic mutation plus compatible clinical features or histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of biochemical, genetic, and histopathological data.

searchTerms: enlarged liver and spleen from fat buildup

pathognomonic.symptomName: Foamy macrophages in bone marrow or tissue biopsy
searchTerms: foamy immune cells in bone marrow

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive neurodegeneration with lipid storage in CNS
searchTerms: worsening brain function from fat buildup
brain decline due to lipid accumulation

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: failure to gain weight or grow

common.symptomName: Coarse facial features due to lipid deposition
searchTerms: coarse facial appearance from fat deposits
facial changes due to lipid buildup
heart muscle disease with fat infiltration

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary infiltrates secondary to lipid accumulation
Seizures related to cerebral lipid storage
searchTerms: seizures caused by brain lipid storage
epilepsy related to fat buildup in brain

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to lipid deposition in auditory pathways
searchTerms: hearing loss from fat deposits in ear
auditory impairment due to lipid storage
deafness related to fat in hearing pathways

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain from lipid infiltration of bone marrow
searchTerms: bone pain from fat in marrow
aching bones due to lipid infiltration

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations such as psychosis or depression
Renal impairment due to lipid accumulation in glomeruli
searchTerms: impaired kidney function due to lipids

laboratory: Reduced activity of lysosomal enzymes (e.g., glucocerebrosidase, sphingomyelinase)
Elevated plasma lipid substrates or metabolites
Abnormal lipid profiles with accumulation of sphingolipids or cholesterol esters
imaging: MRI showing cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with white matter changes
Chest X-ray or CT showing pulmonary infiltrates
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as GBA, SMPD1, NPC1, or others depending on subtype
other: Histopathology revealing lipid-laden macrophages (foam cells) in bone marrow or affected tissues
Electron microscopy showing characteristic lipid inclusions

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic Gaucher cells with wrinkled cytoplasm
Sphingomyelinase deficiency in types A and B
Presence of cherry-red macula and foam cells

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurodegeneration in infancy or early childhood
Presence of cherry-red spot on ophthalmologic exam
references: National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Lipid Storage Diseases
Molecular Genetics and Metabolism, 2022; Lipid Storage Disorders: Clinical and Molecular Aspects
